statement: Every directed edge has string endpoints from and to and an integer cost >= 2. Shortest paths are defined recursively by edge(a, b, c) -> path(a, b, min(c)) and edge(a, b, c1), path(b, c, c2) -> path(a, c, min(c1 + c2)). Define a function of a lower bound k (an integer) that proves by rule induction whether every derived path row across all valid graphs has cost >= k and checks the resulting proof with the proof kernel, returning true when proved and valid and false otherwise. The program's value is the function.
origin: Rule induction over an inductive relation (CIC inductive predicates + kernel checking)
